> Written for blit386 1.8.0, which is not on npm yet. The newest release is 1.7.1, so an API on this page may be missing from the version npm installs until 1.8.0 ships.

Live version: https://demos.blit386.dev/pointer-basics. This is the demo-site source, not a standalone file: it imports and calls helpers from `./shared/` (themed panels, on-screen D-pad, post-process fallbacks), which are not part of blit386 and are not on npm. To run it as is, keep those files from https://github.com/blit386/blit386/tree/main/packages/demos/src/shared at the same relative path. To adapt it, remove or replace the helper imports and every call to them.

```js title="pointer-basics.js"
/*

Pointer Basics: read mouse position, buttons, movement delta, and the scroll wheel.
@description Read mouse position, movement delta, scroll wheel, and four pointer buttons, with a live crosshair.

Part of the BLIT386 demo series.

Prerequisites:
  - Basics: https://demos.blit386.dev/basics
  - Primitives: https://demos.blit386.dev/primitives

Live version: https://demos.blit386.dev/pointer-basics

Guides:
  - Input: https://blit386.dev/docs/guides/input#position-and-delta

Reference:
  - Core: https://blit386.dev/docs/api/core#hardware-settings

---

WHAT YOU WILL SEE
-----------------

A dark screen with a title strip across the top and two equal panels just below it. On
the left, live readouts for pointer slot 0 - whether it is active, its position, how far
it moved this frame, how far the wheel turned, and a meter that fills as you scroll
down. On the right, four pips labeled A to D that light up while the matching mouse
button is held, and a count of the touch slots (1-3) in use.

A white crosshair follows your mouse (or your finger), trailing a cyan line through its
last 24 positions. The crosshair stays on top of the panels; the trail passes behind
them. While no pointer is over the canvas, a dim "Move pointer over canvas" hint sits in
the middle of the open space under the panels instead.

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
-------------------

- The pointer slot model: slot 0 is always the mouse, slots 1-3 are fingers (or a pen) in
  the order they touched down.
- BT.isPointerActive(slot) says whether a slot has a live pointer right now.
- BT.pointerPos(slot) and BT.pointerDelta(slot) return the position and the movement
  since the last update, both in display pixels.
- BT.isDown(BT.BTN_POINTER_A, 0) and friends read the four mouse buttons: A is left, B is
  right, C is middle, D is the back or forward button. Touch slots only ever report A.
- BT.pointerScrollDelta is the wheel movement for the current frame. It stays 0 unless
  configure() sets isCapturingPointerScroll: true.
- BT.hideCursor() hides the OS cursor so a drawn crosshair can take its place.
- Pointer state is held state, not an edge, so reading it from render() is safe.

TRY THIS
--------

- Move the mouse over the demo: the crosshair and its trail follow slot 0.
- Hold the left, right, or middle button to light up the A, B, or C pip. A mouse with a
  back or forward button lights up D.
- Spin the scroll wheel to fill or empty the "Scroll pos" meter.
- On a touchscreen, drag a finger to move the crosshair on slots 1-3 (slot 0 stays
  reserved for the mouse). The wheel and the extra buttons have no touch equivalent, so a
  one-line note appears in the bottom-right corner once a touch is seen. Pointer Paint
  (https://demos.blit386.dev/pointer-paint) uses all four slots at once.
- Press the backquote key (`) to open the engine overlay and watch the timing chart.

*/

import { bootstrap, BT, Color32, Rect2i, Vector2i } from 'blit386';

import { applyTheme, FONT_W, ui, UI_ANCHORS } from './shared/ui.js';

/** @typedef {import('blit386').Palette} Palette */

// Scene palette slots. Slot 0 is always transparent. All the UI colors (panels, text,
// meter fill) come from the shared theme installed by applyTheme() in init(), so the demo
// only needs slots for its own artwork: the crosshair and the cyan trail behind it.
const C_CROSSHAIR = 1; // white crosshair that follows the pointer
const C_TRAIL = 2; // cyan trail line behind the crosshair

// Number of past positions remembered for the cursor trail. Each tick we shift in the
// latest position and draw a line through all of them.
const TRAIL_LENGTH = 24;

// Multiplier applied to the raw scroll delta (BT.pointerScrollDelta) before it is added
// to the scroll position. The browser reports scrolling in CSS pixels, which adds up fast
// - shrinking each report to a quarter keeps one wheel click moving the meter a few
// pixels instead of a big jump. update() then clamps the scroll position to the display
// height so the meter fill always stays between empty and full.
const SCROLL_SENSITIVITY = 0.25;

// Layout: two equal panels, 152 pixels wide and 8 apart, sit 4 pixels below the
// 22-pixel title strip and 4 pixels from the screen sides (4 + 152 + 8 + 152 + 4 = 320).
// Both reserve 63 pixels of rows, so they end on the same line. Everything below them is
// open space for the crosshair.
const PANEL_Y = 26;
const READOUTS_W = 152;
const BUTTONS_W = 152;
const PANELS_BOTTOM = PANEL_Y + 22 + 63 + 11;

// Half the length of each crosshair arm, in pixels.
const CROSSHAIR_ARM = 6;

// Demonstrates the basic pointer API: position, delta, scroll wheel, and the four pointer
// buttons (A, B, C, D) on slot 0 (the mouse).
class Demo {
    /** @type {Palette | null} */
    palette = null;

    // Palette slot map returned by applyTheme() - theme.bg, theme.dim, and so on. Filled
    // in init(); used for the screen clear.
    theme = null;

    // Recent positions, oldest first. Each tick we push the current position and drop the
    // oldest, so the trail shows the cursor's recent path. Each entry is [x, y].
    trail = [];

    // Reused for the two crosshair arms and the two ends of each trail segment, so
    // drawing allocates no new objects.
    armRect = new Rect2i(0, 0, 0, 0);
    lineFrom = new Vector2i(0, 0);
    lineTo = new Vector2i(0, 0);

    // Accumulated scroll position in display pixels. Centered in init() from
    // BT.displaySize. BT.pointerScrollDelta pushes it up or down, and the scroll meter in
    // the readouts panel shows it as a 0..1 fill.
    scrollPos = 0;

    // Turns on wheel capture and the overlay timing chart.
    configure() {
        return {
            // Opt into canvas wheel capture so BT.pointerScrollDelta works and the page
            // does not scroll while the pointer is over the demo.
            isCapturingPointerScroll: true,
            isOverlayEnabled: false,
        };
    }

    // Runs once at startup. Sets up the palette and prefills the trail.
    async init() {
        this.palette = BT.paletteCreate(256);

        // Scene colors: just the crosshair and its trail. Everything else on screen
        // (panels, labels, the meter) is drawn by the shared UI kit.
        this.palette.set(C_CROSSHAIR, new Color32(255, 255, 255));
        this.palette.set(C_TRAIL, new Color32(80, 200, 255));

        // Install the shared UI colors (slots 240-251) and keep the slot map so we can
        // clear with the theme background and reuse the dim text color for the hint.
        this.theme = applyTheme(this.palette);

        BT.paletteSet(this.palette);

        const screen = BT.displaySize;
        this.scrollPos = Math.floor(screen.y / 2);

        // Hide the native OS cursor so the drawn crosshair is the only cursor visible
        // while the pointer is over the canvas.
        BT.hideCursor();

        // Prefill the trail with the center point so the very first frame has something
        // to draw without a special-case "no history yet" path.
        for (let i = 0; i < TRAIL_LENGTH; i++) {
            this.trail.push([Math.floor(screen.x / 2), Math.floor(screen.y / 2)]);
        }

        return true;
    }

    // Per-tick update: push the current pointer position into the trail and apply the
    // scroll-wheel delta to the accumulated scroll position.
    update() {
        // Let the UI kit do its per-tick housekeeping first. This demo asks the kit
        // whether a touchscreen has been used (ui.hasTouch() in render()), and that
        // answer is kept fresh here.
        ui.tick();

        // Only record the trail when a pointer is over the canvas. The mouse uses slot 0;
        // touches use slots 1-3. If none are active, keep the previous trail intact so
        // the line does not snap to (0, 0).
        const slot = this.activePointerSlot();

        if (slot >= 0) {
            const pos = BT.pointerPos(slot);

            // Drop the oldest sample and append the new one.
            this.trail.shift();
            this.trail.push([pos.x, pos.y]);
        }

        // Convert the scroll delta (CSS pixels of scrolling) into a small movement.
        // Multiplying by a fraction makes one wheel click move the meter a few pixels
        // instead of jumping a full screen height.
        this.scrollPos += BT.pointerScrollDelta * SCROLL_SENSITIVITY;

        // Keep the scroll position inside the visible range, using the display height
        // rather than a hard-coded 240.
        const maxScrollY = BT.displaySize.y;

        if (this.scrollPos < 0) {
            this.scrollPos = 0;
        } else if (this.scrollPos > maxScrollY) {
            this.scrollPos = maxScrollY;
        }
    }

    // Per-frame render: clear, draw the UI kit panels (readouts and button pips), then
    // the cursor trail and the crosshair. The trail is plain lines, which the engine
    // draws before every sprite, so it passes behind the panels; the crosshair is drawn
    // as kit sprites after the panels, so the "cursor" is never hidden behind one.
    render() {
        // Clear to the shared theme background so this demo matches the rest of the
        // series.
        BT.clear(this.theme.bg);

        // Full-width title strip with the one-line instructions.
        ui.begin(UI_ANCHORS.TOP_BAR);
        ui.panel('Pointer Basics - move, click, spin the wheel');
        ui.end();

        this.renderReadouts();
        this.renderButtonPips();
        this.renderTouchNote();
        this.renderTrail();
        this.renderCrosshair();
        this.renderPointerHint();
    }

    // Readouts panel in the top-left: pointer position, delta, wheel delta, whether slot
    // 0 is active, and a meter showing the accumulated scroll position. The raw
    // BT.pointer* reads here are the whole point of the demo - pointer state (unlike
    // keyboard edges) is safe to read from render().
    renderReadouts() {
        // Is the mouse currently over the canvas?
        const active = BT.isPointerActive(0);

        // How far the wheel moved this frame (positive = scrolling down).
        const scroll = BT.pointerScrollDelta;

        // The panel starts just below the title strip, at a fixed width so its edge does
        // not jump while the numbers in it change length.
        ui.begin(UI_ANCHORS.TOP_LEFT, { y: PANEL_Y, width: READOUTS_W });
        ui.panel('Slot 0 (mouse)');

        ui.kv('Active', active ? 'yes' : 'no');

        // Only read position and delta when the pointer is over the canvas. The engine
        // keeps the last known values after the mouse leaves, so they would be stale.
        if (active) {
            const pos = BT.pointerPos(0);
            const delta = BT.pointerDelta(0);

            ui.kv('Pos', `${pos.x},${pos.y}`);
            ui.kv('Delta', `${delta.x},${delta.y}`);
        } else {
            ui.kv('Pos', '--,--');
            ui.kv('Delta', '--,--');
        }

        // toFixed(1) turns the number into text with one digit after the decimal point,
        // so the readout does not jitter through long fractions.
        ui.kv('Wheel', scroll.toFixed(1));

        // The meter fills up as you scroll down and empties as you scroll up. Dividing by
        // the display height turns 0..240 pixels into the 0..1 fraction the meter
        // expects.
        ui.meter('Scroll pos', this.scrollPos / BT.displaySize.y, { width: READOUTS_W - 20 });

        ui.end();
    }

    // Buttons panel in the top-right: four read-only pips, one per pointer button, and
    // a count of the touch slots in use. A pip lights up while its button is held and
    // goes hollow when released. BT.isDown() checks held state, which is safe from
    // render().
    renderButtonPips() {
        ui.begin(UI_ANCHORS.TOP_RIGHT, { y: PANEL_Y, width: BUTTONS_W });
        ui.panel('Buttons');

        // Each pip pairs a label with the live held state of one button code.
        ui.pip('A (left)', BT.isDown(BT.BTN_POINTER_A, 0));
        ui.pip('B (right)', BT.isDown(BT.BTN_POINTER_B, 0));
        ui.pip('C (middle)', BT.isDown(BT.BTN_POINTER_C, 0));
        ui.pip('D (extra)', BT.isDown(BT.BTN_POINTER_D, 0));

        // How many fingers are down right now: slots 1-3 are the touch slots. The
        // 13-pixel gap above it makes this panel's rows add up to the same 63 pixels as
        // the readouts panel beside it (4 pips x 10 + 13 + 10).
        let touches = 0;

        for (let slot = 1; slot < 4; slot++) {
            if (BT.isPointerActive(slot)) {
                touches++;
            }
        }

        ui.spacer(13);
        ui.kv('Touches', touches);

        ui.end();
    }

    // A dim one-line note shown only after a touchscreen has been used. Fingers can move
    // the crosshair, but there is no touch equivalent of the scroll wheel or the extra
    // mouse buttons - better to say so than to let touch users hunt for something that
    // cannot happen.
    renderTouchNote() {
        if (!ui.hasTouch()) {
            return;
        }

        // A borderless group (no ui.panel call) is just floating text.
        ui.begin(UI_ANCHORS.BOTTOM_RIGHT);
        ui.label('Scroll wheel and right-click: desktop only', { color: 'dim' });
        ui.end();
    }

    // A line through the recent pointer positions, all drawn in C_TRAIL.
    renderTrail() {
        if (this.activePointerSlot() < 0) {
            return;
        }

        for (let i = 1; i < this.trail.length; i++) {
            const [ax, ay] = this.trail[i - 1];
            const [bx, by] = this.trail[i];
            this.lineFrom.set(ax, ay);
            this.lineTo.set(bx, by);
            BT.drawLine(this.lineFrom, this.lineTo, C_TRAIL);
        }
    }

    // Crosshair drawn at the current pointer position. Only shown while a mouse (slot 0)
    // or touch (slots 1-3) pointer is over the canvas.
    renderCrosshair() {
        const slot = this.activePointerSlot();

        if (slot < 0) {
            return;
        }

        const pos = BT.pointerPos(slot);

        // Two 1-pixel-thick arms that cross at the pointer, each 13 pixels long (6 on
        // either side plus the center pixel). They are drawn with ui.drawRectFill(), the
        // sprite version of BT.drawRectFill(): the engine draws every BT.drawLine() and
        // BT.drawRectFill() before any sprite, and the kit panels are sprites, so a plain
        // line would vanish under a panel whenever the pointer moved over one.
        const span = CROSSHAIR_ARM * 2 + 1;

        this.armRect.set(pos.x - CROSSHAIR_ARM, pos.y, span, 1);
        ui.drawRectFill(this.armRect, C_CROSSHAIR);
        this.armRect.set(pos.x, pos.y - CROSSHAIR_ARM, 1, span);
        ui.drawRectFill(this.armRect, C_CROSSHAIR);
    }

    // "Move pointer over canvas" hint, centered in the open space under the panels.
    // Only shown while no mouse or touch pointer is over the canvas, so newcomers know
    // what to do. Uses the theme's dim text color so it matches the rest of the UI.
    renderPointerHint() {
        if (this.activePointerSlot() >= 0) {
            return;
        }

        // The open space runs from the bottom of the panels to the bottom of the screen.
        // Every character of the system font is FONT_W (6) pixels wide, so starting the
        // text half its width left of the middle centers it; a caption's capital letters
        // cover 7 rows starting 1 row above the y it is given, so centerY - 2 centers
        // them vertically.
        const text = 'Move pointer over canvas';
        const screen = BT.displaySize;
        const centerX = Math.floor(screen.x / 2);
        const centerY = Math.floor((PANELS_BOTTOM + screen.y) / 2);

        ui.caption(centerX - (text.length * FONT_W) / 2, centerY - 2, text, { color: 'dim' });
    }

    // First active pointer slot this frame: mouse (0) preferred, then touch (1-3).
    // Returns -1 when no pointer is over the canvas.
    activePointerSlot() {
        if (BT.isPointerActive(0)) {
            return 0;
        }

        for (let slot = 1; slot < 4; slot++) {
            if (BT.isPointerActive(slot)) {
                return slot;
            }
        }

        return -1;
    }
}

bootstrap(Demo);
```
